java.lang.AssertionError: expected:<502> but was:<200>
	at com.snoworca.naruserve.proxy.ProxyTrustCertificatesTest.assertConnectFailed(ProxyTrustCertificatesTest.java:447) — ./gradlew -PtinyHttpdFromMaven=true :NaruServe-proxy:test --tests 'com.snoworca.naruserve.proxy.ProxyTrustCertificatesTest' at a35977d: 35 tests, 1 failure (this one). Control LP-2 shows the platform rejects the [leaf, X] chain with only the valid CA given (basic constraints check failed: this is not a CA certificate); with only the expired anchor given the code rejects it. So the 200 comes from: platform PKIXValidator drops X (same subject and key as the given expired certificate) and validates [leaf] against the expired anchor (PKIX does not check anchor validity); then checkPathValidity's BFS links leaf -> X (valid, signature verifies) and X is issued by the valid given CA, so reachesValidEnd returns true although X is not a CA and that path is one the platform rejects. The expired given anchor is the only anchor of the path actually validated.

rows.note: Control for LP-1: [crossLeaf, non-CA copy issued by the CA] with only caPem given is 502 CONNECT_FAILED (platform: basic constraints check failed).
[crossLeaf, crossByExpiredCa, non-CA copy] with expiredCa+ca given: 502 (the platform's PKIX builder already refuses; doBuild does not anchor on the expired CA here).
Same as LP-3 with the non-CA copy first: 502.

No-reach branch probe: a valid leaf with the subject and key of the expired given self-signed certificate, issued by an untrusted CA, served alone: 502 on the JVM (PKIXValidator only takes chain[0] as trusted by equality, and the builder finds no anchor). Android's TrustManagerImpl matches a leaf to an anchor by subject and public key, which this branch would then follow; not testable on the JVM, recorded without a finding.
False-reject probe: [leaf, expired intermediate, renewed intermediate (same name and key, valid)] with caPem: reached.
Same as LP-6 with the renewed copy first: reached.
